identity.title: NOVA: A Benchmark for Rare Anomaly Localization and Clinical Reasoning in Brain MRI

problem.claim: Evaluate whether models can detect, localize, caption, and reason about rare, previously unknown brain-MRI anomalies under distribution and semantic shifts.

gap.claim: Common-outlier benchmarks can mask failures on rare or genuinely novel clinical conditions by reducing evaluation to a closed-set problem.

contributions.claim: NOVA is an evaluation-only benchmark of approximately 900 brain-MRI scans covering 281 rare pathologies and heterogeneous acquisition protocols.
The benchmark provides rich clinical narratives and double-blinded expert bounding-box annotations for joint assessment of localization, captioning, and diagnostic reasoning.
It reports baseline results for GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, and Qwen2.5-VL-72B on this stress test.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present NOVA as a challenging, real-life, evaluation-only testbed targeting truly unknown anomalies across appearance and semantic distribution gaps.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report approximately a 65% localization gap relative to natural-image benchmarks.
The authors report approximately 40% and 20% gaps in captioning and reasoning, respectively, relative to resident radiologists.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deployed models encounter inputs unlike their training data, including emerging unknown categories.
Limited common-outlier test sets can conceal failures on rare or novel clinical conditions.
NOVA supplies rare-pathology brain MRIs, clinical narratives, and expert localization annotations for three linked capabilities.
Because it is not used for training, NOVA tests both appearance and semantic shifts; reported baselines show substantial performance gaps.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns benchmark construction with the intended failure modes by combining rare pathologies, heterogeneous protocols, narratives, and localization annotations.

lessons.interpretation: A task-specific evaluation can make the target distribution shift and required capabilities explicit.
lessons.application: When introducing a benchmark, map each claimed failure mode to concrete data variation and an evaluation signal.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when the target task has no reliable annotations or when broad comparability requires a standardized distribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact evaluation metrics, dataset split, or statistical uncertainty.
The meanings of the reported percentage gaps and the underlying benchmark values are not defined.
It does not report per-pathology or per-protocol performance, nor comparisons with additional baselines.
